title: ATS-Job-Pulse input
description: Give a list of companies. For each one the Actor finds its job board (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, Recruitee or SmartRecruiters), returns the open jobs plus a hiring summary, and reports what changed since the previous run. Use the filters to keep the output small.

companies.title: Companies
companies.description: Company website domains (e.g. "stripe.com") or job-board slugs (e.g. "stripe"). To force a specific ATS, prefix the slug: "greenhouse:stripe", "lever:spotify", "ashby:linear", "workable:huggingface", "recruitee:bunq", "smartrecruiters:BoschGroup". Each successfully processed company is charged once, regardless of how many jobs it has.

output_mode.title: What to return
output_mode.description: "jobs_and_summary": one company_summary record per company followed by its job records. "summary_only": only the company_summary records (job counts, new/closed counts, departments, locations, technologies) — the smallest output, best for a quick hiring-signal check. "jobs_only": only job records. For a cheap agent check use output_mode="summary_only" and max_jobs_per_company=20. This keeps returned data small; the per-company charge is unchanged.

track_diff.title: Track changes between runs
track_diff.description: Compare with the previous run that used the same "state_id" and set each job's "status" to NEW, EXISTING or CLOSED. On the first run every job is NEW (the summary marks this with is_first_run = true). When off, every job has status ACTIVE and nothing is remembered.

state_id.title: State ID
state_id.description: Name of the saved history used for change tracking. Runs that share a state_id are compared with each other. Use a different value per watchlist or per schedule.

extract_tech_keywords.title: Extract technology keywords
extract_tech_keywords.description: Scan each job title and description for core technologies (Python, AWS, React, Kubernetes, LLMs, ...) and return them in "detected_technologies" and in the summary's "top_technologies".

only_changes.title: Only new and closed jobs
only_changes.description: Return only jobs whose status is NEW or CLOSED. Use it on scheduled runs to get just what changed since the last run.
only_changes.sectionDescription: Filters reduce which job records are returned. They never affect change tracking or the company summary, which always cover all jobs.

title_keywords.title: Job title contains
title_keywords.description: Return only jobs whose title contains at least one of these words or phrases (case-insensitive). Example: ["engineer", "data scientist"].

departments.title: Department contains
departments.description: Return only jobs whose department contains at least one of these words (case-insensitive). Example: ["engineering", "sales"].

locations.title: Location contains
locations.description: Return only jobs whose location contains at least one of these words (case-insensitive). Example: ["london", "new york", "germany"].

technologies.title: Mentions technology
technologies.description: Return only jobs that mention at least one of these technologies, using the names from "detected_technologies" (case-insensitive). Example: ["Python", "Kubernetes", "LLMs"].

remote_only.title: Remote jobs only
remote_only.description: Return only jobs marked or described as remote.

max_jobs_per_company.title: Max jobs per company
max_jobs_per_company.description: Maximum number of job records returned per company, after the other filters. 0 means no limit. When the limit cuts the list, NEW jobs are kept first, then CLOSED, then the rest. The summary's "matching_jobs" tells how many matched in total. For a cheap agent check use output_mode="summary_only" and max_jobs_per_company=20. This keeps returned data small; the per-company charge is unchanged.
